title: The regulator moves the deadline
setting: Predictive project to put new allergen labels on every product at a food manufacturer. Baselines are approved, and a change board of the PM, the quality lead and the sponsor decides baseline changes.

steps.line: I'm Theo, assistant PM on the allergen-label project at a food plant. Leah is the PM, and we run a predictive plan with approved baselines.
Changes to the baselines go to our change board: Leah, Marco from quality, and Nadia, our sponsor. I keep the schedule up to date.
News this morning: the regulator has brought its labelling deadline forward six weeks. Our current plan finishes four weeks after the new date.
Before anything else, I email Nadia and ask her to approve weekend overtime and two contract designers.

error.summary: Asked the sponsor for resources before assessing the change
error.why: Telling the sponsor early is good, but asking for resources before anyone has read the notice or looked at options is premature. A sponsor needs facts, impact and options to make a sound call.
error.correctAction: Give Nadia a short heads-up that the date moved and an impact assessment is under way, then analyse the notice and options and bring her a recommendation.
error.consequence: Nadia approved overtime that turned out not to be needed for the design work, then questioned the team's later estimates because the first ask had been a guess.

steps.line: I read the regulator's notice in full, and confirm with Marco exactly which products and label details are affected.
The team and I list options: run artwork and printing in parallel, label the top sellers first, or add a second print supplier.
Running in parallel looks best, so I update the schedule baseline myself and send the new dates out to the team.

error.summary: Changed the schedule baseline without the change board
error.why: Even a mandatory change goes through change control. The board must weigh cost, risk and quality impacts, approve the new baseline, and own the decision. An assistant PM can't re-baseline alone.
error.correctAction: Write up the parallel option with its cost, risk and quality impacts and send it to the change board, asking for a fast decision because of the regulatory date.
error.consequence: Marco found that parallel printing skipped a proof check he needed. The team reworked a week of artwork, and the board had to re-baseline twice.

steps.line: Leah asks me to log the label-printer delivery as a risk. I add it with Marco as owner and a backup supplier as the response.
The new printers will arrive a week after the deadline. I tell the plant to keep shipping with old labels that week and relabel stock later.

error.summary: Planned to ship products with non-compliant labels
error.why: Shipping after the deadline with old labels breaks the regulation, and allergen labels protect people's health. Missing a legal requirement isn't a schedule trade-off the project can make on its own.
error.correctAction: Treat it as a compliance issue: raise it with Leah and the change board now, use the backup supplier or interim compliant labels, and let the sponsor and quality decide with legal advice.
error.consequence: A batch went out without the new allergen warning. A customer with an allergy reacted, the company recalled the batch, and the regulator opened an investigation.

steps.line: I prepare a one-page summary for the board: the new date, the options, costs, risks and my recommendation.
Once the board decides, I'll update the plan and brief the plant supervisors on the new order of work.
